title.value: Challenging Common Assumptions of Catastrophic Forgetting
title.justification: The main focus of the paper is to explore the assumptions surrounding catastrophic forgetting in continual learning scenarios, specifically addressing the role of stochastic gradient descent in learning sequences of tasks.
title.quote: This article explores continual learning (CL) on long sequences of tasks sampled from a finite environment... This is in contrast to the current notion of forgetting from the CL literature.

extractions.description: The paper investigates the phenomenon of catastrophic forgetting in deep neural networks when trained with gradient descent over long sequences of tasks. It challenges the assumption that such forgetting is inevitable, proposing a framework called SCoLe to study knowledge retention and accumulation when tasks reoccur. The experiments demonstrate that instead of catastrophic forgetting, stochastic gradient descent can lead to knowledge accumulation over time, especially when data reoccurrence is frequent.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily addresses a technical challenge in deep learning concerning catastrophic forgetting, which is not directly linked to sustainable development. Although understanding DL mechanisms can have implications for sustainability in long-term learning scenarios, the paper does not explicitly connect its findings to climate or ecological themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Continual learning (CL) aims to design algorithms that learn from non-stationary sequences of tasks... Classical challenge in CL is catastrophic forgetting.
